sections.title: Headline
sections.content: The 26 November batch contains 14 notable papers across molecular biophysics, RNA design, computational biology, and medical imaging. The strongest recurring thread is computational modeling that makes hidden constraints explicit—from molecular binding and RNA fold-back to cell-state deconvolution and lesion-preserving reconstruction. This is a relevance-ranked notable-paper selection, not a measured popularity chart.
sections.global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is a relevance-ranked snapshot based on incomplete attention signals and incomplete biomedical coverage. It does not cover bioRxiv, medRxiv, or the broader biomedical literature.

sections.title: Exclusion and internal structure in the association/dissociation kinetics of DNA-binding proteins in the fast diffusion limit
sections.abstract: The authors derive a reduced stochastic and mean-field model for fast-diffusing, multi-state proteins binding DNA with steric exclusion, and fit it to previously measured RPA–ssDNA dynamics.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that a coarse-grained continuous-time Markov model and its mean-field limit capture footprint size and conformational switching, reproduce prior RPA binding dynamics, and represent facilitated exchange in multisegment binding.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a theoretical model checked against simulations and previously measured RPA data, not a new biochemical experiment; the fast-diffusion assumptions and broader applicability require system-specific validation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.75; 3 cross-lists, including q-bio.BM and q-bio.QM. No external attention component was recorded for this candidate.

sections.title: KnitNet: Learning to Search at Inference Time for Exact RNA Inverse Design
sections.abstract: KnitNet uses folding-verifier feedback and coordinated sequence edits to search for RNA sequences whose predicted folds exactly match target structures.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across five secondary-structure benchmarks, the authors report a 21-percentage-point average gain in exact solve rate over continued sampling with 70% less time-to-solve; they also report computational results on pseudoknots and 3D fold-back self-consistency.
sections.unique_caveat: Exactness is defined by computational folding verifiers; the paper does not establish that designed sequences adopt the target structures or functions in laboratory assays.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.50; 2 cross-lists. No external attention component was recorded for this candidate.

sections.title: From the Deterministic Hook Effect to Stochastic Reliability in Ternary Complex Formation
sections.abstract: Deterministic equations and exact stochastic simulations show how mediator dose, reaction volume, and copy-number thresholds can make ternary-complex formation unreliable despite a favorable mean response.
sections.claimed_contribution: In a minimal reversible binding network, the author reports that stochastic reliability windows depend on compartment volume and threshold, and that faster ternary completion or slower breakup can improve modeled reliability.
sections.unique_caveat: The author explicitly frames the network as a deliberately minimal model, not a prediction for a particular drug, assay, or intracellular pathway; no experimental measurements are reported.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.50; 2 cross-lists, including q-bio.BM and q-bio.MN. No external attention component was recorded.

sections.title: MolGPAO: Molecular Generative Pre-trained Autoregressive Octree with Speculative Decoding and Sub-Millisecond Seam Healing for 3D Molecules
sections.abstract: MolGPAO proposes an autoregressive 3D molecular-generation model with octree decoding and geometric refinement, evaluated on drug-like molecule and quantum-chemistry benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved generated-molecule validity and computational efficiency on GEOM-Drugs and QM9, plus DFT-based comparisons on OE62; reported figures are benchmark results, not drug efficacy.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is computational and benchmark-specific; generated structures and property estimates do not demonstrate synthesis, biological activity, safety, or therapeutic value.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.50; 2 cross-lists, including q-bio.BM. The score reflects cross-listing only for this candidate.

sections.title: Escape Time with Quenched Extrinsic Fluctuations in Positive Feedback Systems
sections.abstract: A theoretical framework combines intrinsic biochemical noise with slowly varying cell-to-cell parameter heterogeneity to estimate switching-time statistics in two bistable gene-regulation motifs.
sections.claimed_contribution: For positive autoregulation and a genetic toggle switch, the authors report that extrinsic parameter variability can substantially alter mean escape times and increase their dispersion across modeled cells.
sections.unique_caveat: The results are theoretical and depend on the selected motifs and parameter distributions; they are not observations of a biological cell population.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.00; no external attention or cross-list component was recorded. Zero is not evidence of low scientific importance.

sections.title: Cell-Type-Specific Expression Is Hard to Predict from Bulk, but It Is Still Useful
sections.abstract: The authors derive accuracy limits for cell-type deconvolution and test whether cell-type-specific expression features from bulk RNA data retain prognostic value in non-small-cell lung cancer.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors derive closed-form R² bounds and assess 106 curated cell-type/gene pairs; in an NSCLC overall-survival analysis, a sparse model using deconvolved features performs comparably to one using bulk genes while attributing signals to cell types.
sections.unique_caveat: The survival result is a modeling analysis, not prospective clinical validation; selected targets were found post hoc to have higher learnability scores.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.50; 2 cross-lists. The arXiv record states acceptance at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI for Drug Discovery (AI4DD); this is publication-status context, not an attention measure.

sections.title: Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao Reconstruction of Discrete space Population Dynamics
sections.abstract: The paper extends dynamic Wasserstein–Fisher–Rao transport to discrete states and uses it to reconstruct coarse-grained cell-state dynamics from sparse snapshots.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors derive a closed-form discrete-space solution and propose unbalanced discrete flow matching for larger or more general settings; numerical experiments and real-data applications are reported as plausibility checks.
sections.unique_caveat: Reconstructed trajectories are inferred from sparse observations under modeling assumptions; biological plausibility is not direct evidence that the inferred path is uniquely correct.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.50; 2 cross-lists, including q-bio.PE and q-bio.QM. No external attention component was recorded.

sections.title: Using waveform types, discrete Sobolev distances, and trend compatibility to cluster short time series of clinical data
sections.abstract: A trend-aware clustering method identifies response patterns in short oral-glucose-tolerance-test curves, applied to 1,283 five-point tests.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report seven glycemia and eight insulinemia response types from 1,283 five-point OGTT records; resampling and comparisons with six classical clustering methods are described.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an analysis of cohort-level curve patterns, not an individual diagnostic method; the reported clusters do not establish clinical utility or causal physiology.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.50; 2 cross-lists. No external attention component was recorded.

sections.title: Do Not Let the Prior Heal the Anomaly: Selective Anchoring for Detection from Incomplete Measurements
sections.abstract: Selective anchoring constrains generative image reconstruction to preserve reliably measured components, with reported lesion-preservation and detection results across sparse-view CT, accelerated MRI, and photoacoustic tomography.
sections.claimed_contribution: For accelerated-MRI tumor detection, the authors report that deterministic anchoring raises mean AUROC across eight samplers from 78.4% to 84.6%; on other inverse-imaging tasks they report lesion-contrast and uncertainty improvements.
sections.unique_caveat: These are study-specific reconstruction and detection experiments, not evidence of clinical effectiveness; performance depends on the acquisition, reference, and evaluation setup.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.50; 2 cross-lists, including physics.med-ph. No external attention component was recorded.

sections.title: Did the Model Forecast It, or Already Know It? Evaluating Large Language Models for Novel Drug-Target Prioritisation with a Temporal Knowledge-Graph Oracle
sections.abstract: A temporal knowledge-graph evaluation tests whether six open language models forecast target–disease pairs entering first clinical trials rather than exploit information recorded after the decision date.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across six open LLMs and dated yearly graphs, the authors find that unassisted models rank roughly like trial-history baselines, while newer graph retrieval often leaks the answer through post-decision evidence.
sections.unique_caveat: The result concerns a specific historical target-prioritization benchmark and does not demonstrate prospective drug discovery or clinical success.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.25; 1 cross-list. The record notes acceptance at a NeurIPS 2026 AI4DD workshop; this is not an attention measure.

sections.title: DosePET: An Open-Source Dataset with 2100 Radiation Dose Maps for PET/CT
sections.abstract: DosePET provides 2,100 patient-specific PET/CT absorbed-dose maps generated by Monte Carlo simulation, drawing from examinations at five institutions and seven scanner models.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors describe an open dataset with dose maps, 117 organ/tissue masks per study, regional dosimetry reports, and tools for download and conversion.
sections.unique_caveat: The dose maps are simulation-generated from public PET/CT inputs; their availability does not itself establish dosimetry accuracy or clinical benefit.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.25; 1 cross-list. No external attention component was recorded.

sections.title: Monte Carlo-based secondary dose check platform for the world's first ultra-compact upright proton therapy system
sections.abstract: A TOPAS Monte Carlo model is compared with a treatment-planning system for 15 water-phantom and 25 clinical plans on an upright proton therapy platform.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report agreement with measurements and TPS plans, with all 40 recalculated plans passing the study's point-dose and 3%/2 mm gamma criteria.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a platform-specific secondary-dose comparison; the reported retrospective plan checks do not establish effects on patient outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.00; no external attention or cross-list component was recorded. Zero is not evidence of low scientific importance.

sections.title: Milk-removal feedback shapes lactation sustainability and daily output in a model of human lactation
sections.abstract: A minimal dynamical model compares how milk-removal amount or duration could feed back on production and daily output under alternative removal schedules.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' model predicts that amount-dependent feedback can produce a critical waiting interval or bistability, and that maximizing removal per session need not maximize daily output.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a mathematical model proposed as a basis for testing against longitudinal data, not an empirical study or individualized feeding guidance.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.25; 1 cross-list. No external attention component was recorded.

sections.title: DDxBasis: Explaining Frozen Foundation Encoder-based Medical Classification by Exact Differential Diagnosis
sections.abstract: DDxBasis builds concept-based, differential-diagnosis-style explanations for frozen-encoder medical image classifiers and is evaluated on five medical datasets.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report accuracy competitive with domain-specific results across five datasets and exact decomposition of model decisions into concept evidence; they also report cell-lineage, dermatology-annotation, and shortcut analyses.
sections.unique_caveat: These are retrospective dataset evaluations of classifier explanations, not evidence that the outputs are safe or effective for clinical diagnosis.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Signal score 0.25; 1 cross-list. No external attention component was recorded.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.content: Molecular constraints made explicit: Li and Chou model DNA-protein occupancy and exchange; Agrawal models stochastic ternary-complex reliability; Hernandez-Garcia et al. model gene-network switching under heterogeneity. Learning from structured biological feedback: KnitNet refines RNA sequences from fold errors; Naveh et al. quantify cell-type-specific expression recovery from bulk RNA; Ying et al. reconstruct cell-state dynamics from sparse snapshots. Medical reconstruction and evaluation discipline: Tricard et al. constrain generative imaging; DosePET supplies simulation-derived dose maps; Alakbarzade et al. compare dose calculation with treatment plans. These studies suggest method development, not a field-wide biological shift or clinical validation.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.content: These follow-up directions are synthesis proposals grounded in the selected papers, not claims that the authors proposed or validated these next steps. Prospective biochemical measurements across protein footprints, concentrations, and compartment volumes could test Li and Chou's and Agrawal's modeled regimes beyond fitted or idealized settings. KnitNet's computational fold-back matches could be followed by preregistered synthesis, orthogonal structure assays, and function tests against matched controls, especially for pseudoknots. Independent cohorts and strictly time-stamped held-out data could test whether cell-type deconvolution and target rankings generalize without post-decision leakage. External scanner/site validation and blinded comparisons with independent measurements could extend the imaging and dose work, using domain-expert-prespecified endpoints; these are research proposals, not clinical advice.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's eligible batch spans molecular kinetics, RNA design, computational cell biology, and medical imaging. Its strongest shared contribution is methodological: models make constraints, uncertainty, or information leakage visible. The collected signals support relevance, not a measured popularity verdict.
